name: Nyakim
role: Community midwife, trained at the Leer school
headline: Nyakim walked two days to start training. Today she is the midwife women in her village call first.

portrait.alt: Illustrated portrait of Nyakim, a test persona

quote: When a mother calls me at night, I go. Nobody came for my mother.

chapters.before: Nyakim grew up in a village outside Leer where women gave birth at home, helped only by relatives. When her older sister died in childbirth, she decided she wanted to learn how to keep mothers alive.
chapters.supported: She was selected for the community midwifery course and spent two years learning antenatal care, safe delivery and how to spot danger signs early. After graduating she received a delivery kit and was placed at a health facility close to home.
chapters.changed: Nyakim now runs antenatal visits twice a week and is on call at night. Women who once delivered alone now come to her early in their pregnancy, and she refers difficult cases before they become emergencies.

support.label: Delivery kit and placement
support.detail: Placed at a health facility near her home village

name: Nyaduoth
role: Mother of three, cared for by Nyakim
headline: Her first two babies were born at home. Her third was born with a trained midwife beside her.

portrait.alt: Illustrated portrait of Nyaduoth, a test persona

quote: This time I was not afraid. Someone knew what to do.

chapters.before: Nyaduoth gave birth to her first two children at home. During the second birth she lost a lot of blood, and there was no one nearby who knew how to help.
chapters.supported: In her third pregnancy she attended antenatal visits with Nyakim, who noticed early that the baby was in a difficult position and planned the birth at the health facility.
chapters.changed: Her daughter was born safely. Nyaduoth now brings her sister and neighbours to the clinic when they are pregnant.

support.label: Antenatal care
support.detail: Four visits with a trained midwife

support.label: Facility birth
support.detail: Delivery planned at the health facility

name: Achol
role: Nurse, Presbyterian Health Science Institute graduate
headline: Achol was the first in her family to finish school. Now she runs the children's ward at a county hospital.

portrait.alt: Illustrated portrait of Achol, a test persona

quote: The children I nurse now could be my brothers and sisters. That is why I stay.

chapters.before: Achol grew up between Bor and Juba, moving whenever fighting came close. She finished secondary school late, and could not afford further study.
chapters.supported: She won a place on the nursing diploma at PHSI, with support for fees and accommodation in Juba. Her training included placements on hospital wards.
chapters.changed: After graduating she joined a county hospital, where she now leads the children's ward and trains newer nurses.

impact.label: Children treated on her ward each month

name: Ochan
headline: Ochan's family used to run out of food every rainy season. Last year they had grain to sell.

portrait.alt: Illustrated portrait of Ochan, a test persona

quote: Now my children eat in the hungry months too.

chapters.before: Ochan farms two plots near the river with his wife and five children. Seeds were often eaten before planting, and pests spoiled much of what they stored.
chapters.supported: Through the programme he received improved sorghum and groundnut seed, tools, and training in planting, and joined a farmers' group that shares a storage store.
chapters.changed: His harvest grew, and with better storage the family's grain now lasts through the rainy season. Last year they sold their surplus at the local market.

support.label: Farmer training and group storage
support.detail: Training sessions and a shared grain store

impact.label: Sacks of grain sold last season

name: Nyabol
headline: Nyabol used to spend her mornings fetching water. Now she keeps the village borehole running.

portrait.alt: Illustrated portrait of Nyabol, a test persona

quote: My daughters go to school in the morning now, not to the river.

chapters.before: Every morning Nyabol and her daughters walked to a seasonal pond to collect water, shared with cattle. Children in the village often fell sick with diarrhoea.
chapters.supported: A borehole was drilled at the centre of the village, and Nyabol was elected to the water committee and trained in hygiene promotion and basic repairs.
chapters.changed: Families now collect clean water close to home. Nyabol collects a small monthly fee for repairs and leads hygiene sessions at the school.

name: Deng
role: Father of four, displaced by floods near Bor
headline: The floods took Deng's home and cattle. The family is now rebuilding on higher ground.

portrait.alt: Illustrated portrait of Deng, a test persona

quote: We lost everything in one night. We are standing again, slowly.

chapters.before: When the river rose, Deng's family fled their village with almost nothing. They spent weeks in a crowded site for displaced families.
chapters.supported: The family received shelter materials, household items and food, and the children joined a temporary learning space. Deng took part in community preparedness meetings.
chapters.changed: They have built a new home on higher ground and the children are back in school. Deng now helps his neighbours plan for the next flood season.

name: Gatluak
headline: Gatluak keeps a small clinic open in a place where the nearest hospital is days away.

portrait.alt: Illustrated portrait of Gatluak, a test persona

quote: If the clinic closes, people walk for days. So it does not close.

chapters.before: Gatluak returned to Akobo after years away and found the local clinic without medicines for weeks at a time.
chapters.supported: Through the programme the clinic received regular essential medicines, and Gatluak was trained to treat malaria, pneumonia and diarrhoea in children.
chapters.changed: The clinic now opens every day. Gatluak treats most cases locally and refers only the most serious ones.

impact.label: Days the clinic is open each week
